topics.topic: How to record the triggering actor when a cached admission verdict is reused
questions: When an agent resubmits an existing implementation and its cached verdict is reused, which model records that later agent as the actor whose request triggered the reused admission and automatic activation, or is that triggering action intentionally unrecorded?

quotes: submit_implementation: [ORCHESTRATION] implementation_id is content_identity of the ImplementationContent; a new implementation is written with one RecordImplementationChange under the given actor and submitted_at from kernel_now, an equal existing one writes nothing and is read from the store and used unchanged, its first submitted_by and submitted_at kept (A01 rule 4); then it returns admit_implementation for the new or stored implementation and contract version.

admit_implementation: [BEHAVIOR] MUST act as the kernel actor; when a verdict over the current corpus digest exists for the implementation it is reused and no case executes; otherwise every case of the corpus executes in corpus order through execute_trial_case, never stopping early on a failing case, and one RecordAdmissionVerdictChange records the trial execution ids in corpus order, verdict admitted exactly when the corpus is non-empty and every case passed, otherwise refused with an EmptyCorpusRefusal or a FailingCaseRefusal naming the first case in corpus order that did not pass and its outcome.

admit_implementation: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] An admitted verdict activates the implementation by the kernel in the same request unless it already is the contract version's current activation, read with current_activation before the verdict is written: a new verdict sets activate true in its change exactly when it is admitted and the implementation is not that current activation, otherwise false, an admitted verdict then returning the current Activation and a refused one returning None as the return note says; a reused admitted verdict of an implementation that is not the current activation writes one RecordActivationChange through record_change; a refused verdict activates nothing and leaves the current activation serving.
judgement.why: State 8 explicitly keeps the original implementation submitter, records no new submission or verdict provenance for the later agent, and attributes the automatic activation to the kernel, so the later triggering agent is intentionally unrecorded.

topics.topic: Whether a grown corpus requires a new admission verdict for an existing implementation
questions: When an implementation already has a verdict for an earlier corpus digest and is submitted against a grown corpus, must the kernel compute and record a new verdict for the new implementation–corpus pair?

quotes:
2. Submitting an implementation — new, or equal to an existing one — runs
   admission unless an AdmissionVerdict M08 for that implementation and the
   current corpus digest already exists, in which case that verdict is used. The
   corpus digest is the content identity (State 6, decision 14) of the list of
   its `trial_case_id`s in corpus order.
   Admission executes the implementation on every case of the corpus, in corpus
   order, each as one TrialExecution M07, and never stops early — save for an
   execution whose cleanup cannot be confirmed: it is recorded `crashed` with
   `cleanup_failed` and the kernel stops (A03 rule 7), with no verdict
   recorded; after the restart a submission runs admission afresh.

5. Rollback activates an earlier implementation of the slot's current contract
   version that already holds an `admitted` verdict over the current corpus; it
   runs no admission. Naming the implementation that is already current returns
   the current activation and records nothing. An implementation without such a
   verdict is refused; to
   re-admit an earlier implementation over a grown corpus the agent submits it
   again under rule 2.
judgement.why: State 2 makes verdict lookup specific to both the implementation and current corpus digest, so submission after corpus growth runs admission and records a verdict for the new pair.
